hypotheses.latent_object: S2_master[H1,H2] = Sum over n,m of Piecewise((K2_diag(epsilon(n);beta,gamma,mu)*H1*H2, Eq(m,n)), (K2_gen(epsilon(n),epsilon(m);beta,gamma,mu)*H1*H2, True))
hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: G0002 is S2_master with H1=h1(b,n,m), H2=h2(a,c,m,n); G0006 is S2_master with b<->c swapped in the H factors.
required_assumptions: K2_diag and K2_gen depend on beta, gamma, mu, epsilon(n), epsilon(m) but not on external labels a, b, c except through H1,H2.

proof_obligations.expected: G0006 equals G0002 after swapping b and c in the coefficient factors H1,H2.

hypotheses.scientific_rationale: The two-index sum families share the same polygamma kernel and differ structurally only by the labels carried by h1 and h2 coefficients.

hypotheses.latent_object: S3_master[H1,H2,H3] = Sum over n,m,ell of the piecewise three-index kernel K3(epsilon(n),epsilon(m),epsilon(ell);beta,gamma,mu)*H1*H2*H3
hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: G0010 is S3_master with H1=h1(a,m,n), H2=h1(b,ell,m), H3=h1(c,n,ell); G0017 is S3_master with the index-rotation in H2 and H3 as specified.
required_assumptions: The three-index kernel K3 is shared between the two orientations of the h1 coefficient factors.

proof_obligations.expected: G0017 equals G0010 after the specified rotation of the second and third h1 index arguments.

hypotheses.scientific_rationale: The two three-index sum families are the same master sum with different cyclic ordering of the h1 coefficient indices, exposing a discrete orientation symmetry.

hypotheses.latent_object: K2_gen(p,q;H1,H2) = generic two-index branch kernel from G0005/G0009 with distinct nodes p,q and factors H1,H2
hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: G0005 and G0009 are K2_gen evaluated at p=epsilon(n), q=epsilon(m); G0004 and G0008 are the same generic kernel in the limit q->p.
required_assumptions: The diagonal branch arises by confluence of the two nodes epsilon(m) and epsilon(n).

proof_obligations.expected: G0004 equals lim_{epsilon(m)->epsilon(n)} G0005 with the same H1,H2.
G0008 equals lim_{epsilon(m)->epsilon(n)} G0009 with the same H1,H2.

hypotheses.scientific_rationale: The piecewise structure separates generic unequal indices from the diagonal confluent case, so the diagonal expressions are naturally local coalescence limits of the generic two-index kernel.

hypotheses.latent_object: K3_gen(p,q,r;H1,H2,H3) = generic three-index branch kernel from G0016/G0023 with distinct nodes p,q,r and factors H1,H2,H3
hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: G0016 and G0023 are K3_gen evaluated at p=epsilon(n), q=epsilon(m), r=epsilon(ell); G0012 and G0019 are the limits q->p and r->p of the corresponding generic branches.
required_assumptions: The all-equal branch arises by confluence of the three nodes epsilon(n), epsilon(m), epsilon(ell).

proof_obligations.expected: G0012 equals lim_{epsilon(m)->epsilon(n), epsilon(ell)->epsilon(n)} G0016 with the same H1,H2,H3.
G0019 equals lim_{epsilon(m)->epsilon(n), epsilon(ell)->epsilon(n)} G0023 with the same H1,H2,H3.

hypotheses.scientific_rationale: The triple-index piecewise branches are organized by repeated nodes: the all-equal piece is the confluent limit of the fully generic three-index branch.
